subject: Per-token commit ladder — request for structure and example math
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nimblehealth.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing: per-token discounts & commit tiers

Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our procurement team asked me to follow up with a concrete ask — NimbleHealth is evaluating a two-year commit for hosted API usage and wants to understand two options: 1) a marginal-breakpoint ladder (per-token drop at defined volume bands) and 2) a blended effective-rate approach (single blended per-token across committed volume).

Key constraints:
- We expect bursty production traffic; monthly usage will vary between 100M–900M tokens.
- We need a simple true-up mechanic at quarter-end.
- Prefer minimal invoicing complexity (team prefers a single blended invoice if possible).

Can you send a proposal showing:
- Example math for a three-breakpoint marginal ladder vs blended equivalent for a 12M token monthly commit (144M tokens/year) and a 50% growth scenario?
- How breakpoints affect unit economics and whether clawbacks or credits apply on down-usage?
- Suggested guardrails for bursting and overage handling.

If you have a one-pager or a sample contract clause that demonstrates the mechanics, that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Partnerships
NimbleHealth

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: per-token discounts & commit tiers
Attachments: NIHB-proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary, 2 pages); nimble_cost_model_v2.xlsx (breakpoint math)

Hi Liam — good to reconnect.

Attached is a straw proposal and an accompanying cost model workbook. High-level summary in this thread below. We focused on: clarity for your finance team, a straightforward true-up cadence, and explicit bursting rules.

Option A — Marginal-breakpoint ladder (recommended if you want transparency):
- Breakpoints (monthly): 0–2M, 2M–10M, 10M+ (example bands for illustration)
- Per-token rates (example): $0.00012, $0.000095, $0.000075 respectively (marginal pricing applied to tokens in each band)
- True-up: quarterly true-up against committed monthly average; overage billed at published overage rate (marginal top band + 15%).
- Down-usage: carry-forward credit pool for 2 quarters; netting occurs at quarter true-up.

Option B — Blended effective-rate (preferred by some finance teams):
- Single blended per-token computed by weighting marginal rates against committed volume.
- Simpler invoice line (one rate), but less visibility on marginal unit economics.
- Suggested guardrail: if month-to-month usage deviates >2x from committed monthly baseline, apply short-term burst surcharge to protect SLOs.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Marginal ladder: better for showing marginal cost savings as you grow; more complex invoicing and requires clear clawback language.
- Blended: simpler for billing; can hide tail risk if growth is uneven and you need to renegotiate later.

I called out two illustrative scenarios in the workbook:
1) Conservative: steady 12M monthly commit (baseline)
2) Growth: 18M monthly avg after 6 months (50% uplift) — shows how blended vs marginal play out across months and annualized spend.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right, Marissa / Connor and I can iterate contract language (clawback, true-up, burst credits), and we can produce a redline-friendly SOW for legal.

-Jordan

Looping in finance/legal notes — keeping public copy to Liam so expectations are aligned.

Connor / Jordan — quick comments from my side after reviewing the workbook:
- Breakpoint sizing: recommend anchoring breakpoints to realistic percentiles of your historical token distribution (p50, p75, p95) rather than fixed absolute bands. For NimbleHealth, if p95 is near 14M/mo then the top band should start above that to avoid frequent shock pricing.
- Clawback mechanics: prefer a simple quarterly true-up where down-usage is credited as a cash credit rather than retroactive rate changes. Credits should expire after 2 quarters. If customer materially reduces committed baseline (>30% sustained decline over 2 quarters), include a renegotiation clause.
- Burst policy: allow short bursts up to 2x committed monthly baseline for up to 72 hours without surcharge if we have capacity headroom; otherwise apply 25% overage premium. Document fallback to a lower-capacity model variant to protect latency SLO.
- Examples: in the workbook I added a blended-rate example that shows a 7% difference in year-1 spend between the blended and marginal approach under the growth scenario. (See tab "Scenario_A_vs_B").

I also suggested a compromise structure: a flattened ladder with fewer bands (e.g., 2 breakpoints) plus an annual reconciliation to produce a single blended true-up credit/charge. That tends to be easier to operationalize for both parties.

If Liam is OK, I can draft the SOW language and we can pass to your procurement for redlines.

Best,

Liam — thanks for the clear ask and for looping finance. Quick counterproposal and clarifying math inline so procurement can act quickly.

Counterproposal (two-year commitment, annual true-up):
- Committed baseline: 12M tokens/month (144M tokens/year).
- Offer A (Marginal ladder, monthly):
  * Band 1 (0–4M): $0.00013/token
  * Band 2 (4M–12M): $0.00010/token
  * Band 3 (12M+): $0.000078/token
  * Overage: billed at Band3 rate + 20%
  * Quarterly true-up: unused committed tokens convert to credit carry-forward for 2 quarters; sustained baseline reduction (>30% for two consecutive quarters) triggers renegotiation.

- Offer B (Blended effective rate):
  * Single blended rate computed on committed 12M/mo baseline using marginal ladder weights above = $0.000098/token (in year 1).
  * Simpler single-line invoice. Burst allowance: up to 2x committed month for 72 hours with 25% surcharge if capacity constrained.

Example math (month with 18M tokens):
- Marginal calculation: (4M * 0.00013) + (8M * 0.00010) + (6M * 0.000078) = $520 + $800 + $468 = $1,788 -> effective per-token = $1,788 / 18M = $0.00009933
- Blended calculation (using committed blended rate): 18M * $0.000098 = $1,764 -> effective per-token = $0.00009800
- Difference in that month: marginal effective is ~1.36% higher than blended (growth months can swing direction depending on where tokens fall in bands). Annualized we modeled both scenarios in the workbook — blended tends to slightly favor the customer in steady growth months; marginal rewards stronger high-volume tails.

Operational ask: if you prefer Offer B (blended), procurement should accept a bilateral annual true-up (automated in invoicing) and an explicit bursting clause. If you prefer Offer A (marginal), we will include the credit carry-forward and quarterly reconciliation language in the SOW.

Next steps: pick A or B and we'll send a one-page SOW + contract clause for legal review. Connor, Marissa — please prepare the minimal SOW and a clean redline-friendly clause (no model-level secrets). Liam — happy to hop on a 30-min call if procurement wants to walk through the model.

-Jordan
